claims.exact_wording: The evaluated complex operator has an exact structured real-block implementation that reproduces its top-1 predictions at numerical precision.
evidence: QN-000033 mapped mechanism runs differ by at most approximately 4.8e-7 across recorded metrics.
QN-000042 complex and exact-real top-1 are identical in all 1,920 held-out nested cells; maximum NLL difference is 3.58e-7.
counterevidence: This does not imply that every complex-valued architecture or optimization trajectory is equivalent to every unconstrained real network.
Different parameterizations can impose different inductive biases even when the represented mapped function is the same.

AMENDMENT-001: the two implementations do not merely represent the same function class; they share the same real parameter coordinates. ComplexOperatorState stores only real-valued nn.Parameters and constructs complex tensors inside the forward pass, so the parameter map between the two models is the identity and the observed agreement is a numerical-implementation result rather than a coordinate-transport result.

amendments.effect: narrows interpretation; no numerical value changed
amendments.summary: The complex/exact-real pair is one parameterization with two implementations, not two parameterizations of one function class. Equivalence level is downgraded from implied E1 to E2/E3 on a declared input domain because the two complex-tanh implementations diverge near the pole at i*pi/2.

claims.uncertainty: Deterministic mapped equivalence plus floating-point tolerance; not a population estimate.
claims.external_validity: Algebraic mapping is general; empirical tolerance was tested only in this codebase.
claims.novelty_status: Known algebraic representation applied as a stringent project control.
claims.replication_status: Internally repeated across mechanism discovery and four held-out task families; no independent team replication.
claims.falsifier: A mapped forward, loss, gradient, or prediction comparison exceeding the frozen numerical tolerance.

claims.exact_wording: Within the reduced independent-task studies, the cellwise best-real envelope removes the observed complex robustness advantage.
evidence: QN-000040 has zero positive complex-minus-best-real effects among 2,880 nested discovery cells.
QN-000042 has zero positive effects among 1,920 held-out nested cells and a family/world/seed hierarchical mean of -0.00916 with 95% interval [-0.01325, -0.00457].
counterevidence: The independent discovery and confirmation profiles are outcome-ineligible and compute-reduced.
The complete 14-model real envelope and full ShiftGauntlet outcome grid were not run.

AMENDMENT-001: the 1,920 held-out cells are not 1,920 independent architecture comparisons. The cellwise best-real winner was exact_real_block_operator in 1,478 cells (77%) with mean effect exactly +0.00000 and 1,478 exact zeros, and real_polar_operator in 442 cells (23%) with mean -0.03978. The 1,478 zeros are equivalence-induced ties with an implementation that shares the complex model's parameter coordinates, not independent wins by a distinct real architecture. The entire -0.00916 mean is carried by the 442 real_polar_operator cells.

AMENDMENT-001: QN-000040 is the healthier heterogeneous-control result. There state_space (637 cells, -0.09063), real_polar_operator (485, -0.04687), and gru (367, -0.07073) win 52% of discovery cells against exact_real_block_operator's 1,391.

amendments.effect: strengthens the negative result; no numerical value changed
amendments.summary: The falsification of the intrinsic-complex-arithmetic claim now rests on two explicitly separated legs: exact realification reproduces the implemented computation, and genuinely distinct real controls outperform it. The 1,920-cell headline must distinguish equivalence-induced zeros from independent architecture wins.

assumptions: best-real selection is cellwise and prespecified
claims.scope: Four held-out and four discovery synthetic nonmedical generator families under the reduced profile
claims.external_validity: Unknown beyond the implemented synthetic generators.
claims.novelty_status: Negative empirical result; priority not claimed.
claims.replication_status: Direction repeats in pilot, discovery, and held-out reduced confirmation; no external replication.
claims.falsifier: A fully preregistered clean run in which the complex-minus-best-real aggregate is positive and its adjusted interval exceeds +0.02.

claims.exact_wording: The frozen quadratic relationship selected on reduced discovery data fails quantitative prediction on held-out task families.
evidence: QN-LAW-001 discovery R2 is 0.949 with MAE 0.00260 across 12 aggregate cells.
QN-000042 held-out R2 is -30.94 and MAE 0.0313; the frozen requirements were R2 at least 0.50 and MAE at most 0.015.
counterevidence: Effect-sign accuracy is 1.0 because all observed and predicted gaps are non-positive.
claims.uncertainty: Twelve held-out family-by-severity aggregates; no refitting permitted.
claims.falsifier: Not applicable after prospective failure; a new law requires a new preregistration and split.

claims.exact_wording: The earlier positive NeuroWorld result is comparator-dependent rather than evidence of intrinsically complex arithmetic.
evidence: QN-000008 reports +0.0602 moderate-shift top-1 versus a two-channel real control.
Later exact-real and best-real comparisons reverse the sign in QN-000031, QN-000040, and QN-000042.
counterevidence: The later studies use different generator families and reduced profiles, so the four point estimates are not one meta-analysis.
assumptions: comparator identity is stated with every estimate
claims.scope: Interpretation of the QN-000008 within-simulator result
claims.replication_status: Historical result replicated within NeuroWorld; intrinsic interpretation refuted by stronger controls.
claims.falsifier: A same-task parameter/compute-matched study in which complex exceeds the exact-real and strongest structured-real controls.

claims.exact_wording: QN-GRAND-001 did not execute and provides no primary confirmatory effect estimate.
evidence: The registered preflight records six blocking failures and sealed_benchmark_opened=false.
counterevidence: Eight readiness checks passed, including the shortcut gate, power plan, exact-real equivalence, and held-out family separation.
assumptions: Any failed mandatory gate blocks sealed access
claims.falsifier: Artifact evidence that all gates passed and the sealed benchmark was executed, which does not exist.

claims.exact_wording: The repository contains no evidence of clinical validity, patient benefit, safety, or a quantum mechanism of cognition.
evidence: All next-phase tasks are synthetic and nonclinical; no patient dataset was selected or evaluated.
claims.uncertainty: This is a scope statement, not an efficacy estimate.
claims.falsifier: A separately approved and preregistered clinical validation program with valid patient evidence.

claims.exact_wording: On workloads with a deep worst case and heavy-tailed difficulty, halting on a supervised predicate attains the optimal per-example compute allocation and gives a 2.8-4.9x wall-clock inference saving at batch 1 at matched accuracy and matched parameters, and loses that advantage entirely above batch approximately 32.
evidence: QNEURO3-NICHE-P1 (sha256 7fbcceb87f9a2193) was frozen on the streaming family and opened once on the associative-lookup family at depth 24 with a heavy-tailed distribution never used before. All four clauses passed: accuracy 1.0000 against select's 1.0000; mean steps 6.14 against E[distance] 6.14; batch-1 speedup 2.78x against a required 2.5x; batch-256 speedup 0.97x against a required ceiling of 1.2x.
Mean step count equals E[predicate index] to within 0.1 in six independent settings (4.45/8, 6.55/12, 2.51/4, 4.54/8, 6.60/12, 6.14/24).
Measured crossover curve on the M2: 2.99x at batch 1, 1.58x at 4, 1.18x at 16, 0.99x at 64, 0.97x at 256.
counterevidence: No novelty is claimed. Supervised early exit and per-step attribution are prior art (Graves 2016; Banino et al. 2021; Vinyals et al. 2015; Lee et al. 2015).
The SIZE of the saving is max_depth / E[predicate index], a property of the workload rather than of the architecture. The architecture's contribution is attaining that optimum reliably.
Measured on one machine (Apple M2 CPU) at one model scale. Continuous batching or sequence packing may recover part of the saving above the crossover and was not measured.
Synthetic tasks only.
claims.assumptions: Per-example halt steps are independent across a batch; the halting predicate is supervised by the task; difficulty is heavy-tailed with a deep worst case; inference runs on CPU at the measured model scale.
claims.effect_size: 2.78x mean wall-clock speedup at batch 1 over 25 independent examples (lookup family, depth 24); 4.89x on the streaming family at depth 32; 0.97-0.99x at batch 256 on both. Mean steps 6.14 of 24 against E[distance] 6.14.
claims.external_validity: Two synthetic task families with structurally different cores (attention-based graph traversal, attention-free streaming). One machine, one model scale, CPU only. Not tested on natural data, on GPU, at large model width, or under continuous batching.
claims.falsifier: A matched-accuracy, matched-parameter comparison on a heavy-tailed variable-difficulty workload where batch-1 wall-clock saving is below 1.5x, or where the advantage persists above 1.2x at batch 256.
claims.novelty_status: No novelty claimed. Supervised early exit and per-step attribution are prior art (Graves 2016 ACT; Banino et al. 2021 PonderNet; Vinyals et al. 2015 Pointer Networks; Lee et al. 2015 deeply-supervised nets). The contribution is the measured boundary, not the mechanism.
claims.replication_status: Frozen and confirmed once on an untouched family under QNEURO3-NICHE-P1; 3 seeds per condition; single implementation, no independent reimplementation.
claims.uncertainty: Batch-1 timing on a fanless machine varies with thermal state; the headline is a mean over 25 independent examples with a per-example range of 0.93x to 13.16x. The crossover batch is located between 16 and 64 and is not resolved more finely.

claims.exact_wording: Per-example adaptive computation has an analytic ceiling under batching: because a batch cannot exit until its slowest member does, batched cost tracks E[max halt step over the batch] rather than E[halt step], so the realisable saving decays towards 1 as batch size grows.
evidence: E[max] = sum_k k (F(k)^n - F(k-1)^n). For P(k) proportional to 0.8^k on 1..32: E[max] = 4.97 at batch 1, 12.53 at 8, 20.96 at 64, 29.42 at 1024, so the realisable saving falls from 6.43x to 1.09x.
Measured wall-clock agrees: early exit is 0.96-0.99x at batch 64-256 on both task families, i.e. a penalty.
counterevidence: This is arithmetic about order statistics, not an empirical finding about any particular architecture, and no novelty is claimed for it.
It is stated for independent per-example halt steps. Correlated difficulty within a batch would change the constant, though not the direction.
claims.scope: applies to any per-example adaptive-compute method, including ACT, PonderNet, early-exit transformers and depth-routed mixtures of experts
claims.assumptions: Halt steps are drawn independently and identically across the batch; every example in a batch is processed to the batch's maximum halt step; no continuous batching or sequence packing.
claims.effect_size: For P(k) proportional to 0.8^k on 1..32 the realisable saving falls from 6.43x at batch 1 to 2.55x at 8, 1.53x at 64 and 1.09x at 1024.
claims.external_validity: The derivation is distribution-free; only the constants depend on the halt distribution. It applies to any per-example adaptive-compute method under static batching.
claims.falsifier: A batched implementation whose measured cost tracks E[halt] rather than E[max halt] without continuous batching, or an order-statistics counterexample.
claims.novelty_status: No novelty claimed. This is elementary order statistics; it is recorded because the consequence for adaptive computation is not usually stated alongside reported speedups.
claims.replication_status: Analytic, implemented and unit-tested as qneuro3.adaptive.expected_max_halt; empirically corroborated on two task families.
claims.uncertainty: Correlated difficulty within a batch would change the constants though not the direction; that case is not measured.

claims.exact_wording: Reading a computation's answer from an input-selected iteration rather than from the final state is generally necessary for first-match computations.
evidence: On the associative-lookup family the separation is large and robust: a final-state readout scores 0.221-0.273 against 1.0000, and survives matched per-step supervision (0.232-0.243), an explicit learned latch (0.222-0.239) and 3x training.
counterevidence: QNEURO3-TRANSFER-P1 (sha256 3ef3b2e56d08ca66) was frozen and opened once on a qualitatively different family. The required gap was 0.20; the measured gap was 0.007 in the wrong direction of interest (final-state readout 0.9351 against selection 0.9425). The kill condition applied.
The strongest model on that family is the explicit latch (0.9760), which is one of the controls that failed on the lookup family. The two families reward opposite designs.
claims.scope: the separation is retained as a property of associative-lookup tasks only
claims.assumptions: Matched core, matched per-step inputs, matched per-step supervision, parameters within 0.5%, identical training protocol.
claims.effect_size: Associative lookup: 0.221-0.273 for final-state readout against 1.0000 for input-selected readout. Streaming: 0.9351 against 0.9425, a gap of 0.007.
claims.external_validity: The separation is established on associative-lookup tasks only and explicitly does not transfer to a streaming arithmetic family.
claims.falsifier: Already falsified as a general claim by QNEURO3-TRANSFER-P1. The scoped version would be falsified by an associative-lookup task where a final-state readout matches input-selected readout at matched supervision and compute.
claims.novelty_status: No novelty claimed. Position-selection readouts are Pointer Networks and span scoring.
claims.replication_status: Six readout policies, 2-5 seeds each, one implementation. The generalisation test was frozen and run once.
claims.uncertainty: The sharp fixed-depth capability threshold between max_depth 4 and 8 is unexplained; the frozen carry-distance account was tested and is false.

claims.exact_wording: Predicate halting confers depth extrapolation: a model whose stopping rule is a local condition can iterate correctly beyond the depth it was trained at.
counterevidence: QNEURO3-EXTRAP-P1 (sha256 09aabd9169a7713b) required at least 0.80 accuracy on unseen depths on every seed and measured 0.8328, 0.3528, 0.6548.

Its mechanism clause inverted: the unnormalised model extrapolates at 0.9136 against the normalised model's 0.6135, so state normalisation costs 0.30 of extrapolated accuracy while buying about 0.05 in distribution.
claims.scope: tested on the streaming family at 1.33x the trained depth
claims.assumptions: Trained at length 12 and evaluated without retraining at length 16 on the streaming family; standard protocol; 3 seeds.
claims.effect_size: 0.8328 / 0.3528 / 0.6548 on unseen depths against a required 0.80 on every seed. Unnormalised: 0.8926 / 0.8678 / 0.9803.
claims.external_validity: One family, one extrapolation ratio (1.33x). Not tested on the lookup family or at larger ratios.
claims.falsifier: Already falsified. Reviving it would require a materially different halting mechanism and a new prediction identifier.
claims.novelty_status: Not applicable; the claim is falsified.
claims.replication_status: Frozen once, opened once, 3 seeds per condition.
claims.uncertainty: The inversion of the normalisation clause is measured on 3 seeds per condition and is large (0.30 absolute), but is not explained.
